topic.angle: How crops and diseases reshaped two hemispheres

body.claim: Potatoes, maize and tomatoes crossed the Atlantic after 1492 and changed what the world eats.
body.why: After Columbus's voyage, crops and animals began moving between the hemispheres. American crops such as maize, potatoes, tomatoes, cassava and chili peppers became important worldwide, and helped food production and population grow in the Old World. Wheat, rice, sugar cane and livestock went the other way. The exchange also carried disease: Old World illnesses cut the Indigenous population of the Americas by 80 to 95 percent.

probes.question: Which of these crops came to the rest of the world from the Americas?
True or false: the Columbian exchange moved plants and animals in only one direction.

claims.claim: Maize, potatoes, tomatoes, cassava and chili peppers became important crops worldwide (title, claim, p1)
claims.quote: maize , potatoes , tomatoes , tobacco , cassava , sweet potatoes , and chili peppers became important crops around the world

claims.claim: Crops and livestock interchange supported food production and population growth in the Old World
claims.quote: interchange of many species of crops and livestock , which supported increases in food production and population in the Old World

claims.claim: Wheat, rice, sugar cane and livestock went the other way (p2 false)
claims.quote: Old World rice , wheat , sugar cane , and livestock , among other crops, became important in the New World

claims.claim: Old World illnesses cut the Indigenous population of the Americas by 80 to 95 percent
claims.quote: Communicable diseases of Old World origin resulted in an 80 to 95 percent reduction in the Indigenous population of the Americas
